links.outcome: LLM output quality sensitivity to input serialization format across models
links.effect: Serialization significantly changed quality on both evaluation layers; significant Model x Serializer interaction (Friedman p = 0.0009), with best format differing by model (GPT-5.4 favoring Raw JSON, others compressed formats).
links.quote: Third, a significant Model × Serializer interaction (Friedman p = 0.0009) precludes universal format recommendations, with GPT-5.4 favoring Raw JSON while Claude and open-weight models favor compressed formats.

links.outcome: Inference failure on long, complex patient records within nominal context window
links.effect: Llama 3.1 70B showed 100% inference failure on complex patients despite operating within its nominal context window.
links.quote: Fourth, Llama 3.1 70B exhibits 100% inference failure on complex patients despite operating within its nominal context window, revealing a patient-safety gap where AI assistance fails precisely for the patients who need it most.

unlisted_practices: Multi-layer evaluation combining token-level F1 with LLM-as-judge rubric scoring
Explicit capacity verification for complex patient records before deployment
Choosing token-efficient FHIR serialization formats (e.g., narrative) to reduce cost

screen.practice: FHIR serialization format selection and pre-deployment capacity verification
screen.reason: Evaluates how different input data serialization strategies (formatting/prompting practices for structured FHIR clinical records) affect downstream LLM clinical decision support performance and failure rates.
